propositions: Command syntax is split across reusable argparse parsers, imperative argv loops, 54 hand-maintained package-help files, and 22 curated intercept descriptions, causing command-census drift and disagreement between parser, runtime help, and documentation.
All command grammars must be produced by a single runtime-used side-effect-free argparse factory with no duplicate parsers, regex-based grammars, or second parser frameworks.

Generated package help and grouped overview must be byte-current and produced deterministically from factories, with top-level help forms serving generated bytes before operation/config/store/handler boundaries.
Parser migrations must capture and maintain parity for accepted/rejected argv, --handling, diagnostics, streams, and exit codes between old imperative parsing and new factory-based parsing.

Retired and alias command syntax must be handled through compatibility shims and generated artifacts, with retired syntax remaining undiscoverable while canonical visible commands appear exactly once in generated overview.
